item.title: Adani Flagship Is the Next Big India Pick for Singapore’s Helios
item.description: Helios Capital Management is betting on the flagship stock of India’s Adani Group to be the next big winner for its funds in a market left behind in the global AI frenzy.

item.title: Malaysia’s Anwar to Debut an AI Double That Sounds Just Like Him
item.description: Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is about to do something very few heads of government have done: send an artificial intelligence version of himself out to meet the public.

item.title: Tencent in Talks to Become Manus’ Largest Holder, FT Reports
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd. is in discussions to become the largest shareholder in Manus, the Chinese agentic AI pioneer whose blockbuster acquisition by Meta Platforms Inc. was struck down by Beijing, the Financial Times reported.

item.title: Iron Ore Set For Weekly Gain on BHP Port Strike, FMG Stalemate
item.description: Iron ore was on track for the biggest weekly gain since early May as a looming strike at BHP Group’s Port Hedland terminal stoked supply concerns, even as fundamentals remain tested.

item.title: Rupee May be Tested as RBI Unwinds Bearish Dollar Bets
item.description: Short dollar forward positions ballooned to $106.7 billion in May.

item.title: Modi Visit Showcases New Zealand Leader Luxon’s Trade Coup Ahead of Tight Ballot
item.description: Narendra Modi’s visit to Auckland — the first by an Indian prime minister in four decades — highlights one of New Zealand leader Christopher Luxon’s biggest foreign policy coups: securing a free trade agreement with the world’s most populous nation.

item.title: Strategists Diverge on Long-Term Yen Trend After Katayama Speech
item.description: Some strategists see a boost to assets, while others were sceptical of a sustained rally, following Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama’s comments Friday encouraging pension funds, including the massive Government Pension Investment Fund, to increase investment in domestic financial assets. Here’s what strategists are saying:

item.title: Copper Heads for Weekly Gain as Traders Look Past Iran Flare-Up
item.description: Copper was on track for its second straight weekly gain as investors looked past potential demand headwinds presented by the mid-week resurgence in fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Japan’s Long Bonds, Yen Rise on Push for More GPIF Investment
item.description: Japan’s long-term bond yields fell and the yen strengthened after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said the government wants to encourage pension funds, including the Government Pension Investment Fund, to increase investment in domestic financial assets.

item.title: AI, Iran War Risks Weigh on Indian IT Firms’ Earnings Outlook
item.description: HCL Technologies Ltd., Wipro Ltd. and Tech Mahindra Ltd. are set to report earnings as their investor base increasingly questions the value of traditional IT services in the age of artificial intelligence.

item.title: JPMorgan, Citi Bankers to Join Hong Kong Exchange Listing Panel
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Nelly Pai and Citigroup Inc.’s Alexander Schrantz are joining the Hong Kong stock exchange panel responsible for approving initial public offerings, according to people familiar with the matter, as the city sharpens its scrutiny of deal quality.

item.title: Yuan Gains as PBOC Sets Fix Below 6.8 for First Time Since 2023
item.description: The yuan advanced after China’s central bank signaled its comfort with the currency’s strength by setting the daily reference rate below 6.80 per dollar for the first time since 2023.

item.title: Japan Urges Its Pension Funds to Invest More at Home; Yen Gains
item.description: Japan called on its pension funds, which include one of the world’s largest, to invest in domestic assets, giving a boost to both bonds and the yen from levels near multi-decade lows.

item.title: RBI Faces $100 Billion Challenge After Record Currency Defense
item.description: Over the past two years, India’s central bank built one of the world’s largest bearish dollar bets to support a persistently weak rupee. It now faces the challenge of unwinding that position without destabilizing the currency market.

item.title: China AI Star Zhipu’s ‘Low Float’ Risk Persists After Share Sale
item.description: Zhipu, China’s hottest AI stock, may continue to see wild swings as the company’s $4 billion equities fundraising does little to meaningfully boost its thin pool of publicly tradable shares.

item.title: Prabowo’s Clampdown on Indonesian Tycoons Fuels Capital Flight
item.description: High-net-worth individuals say they fear the president may turn to more forceful measures to extract their money.

item.title: Japan’s Producer Prices Pick Up to Fastest Pace Since Early 2023
item.description: Japan’s corporate goods prices picked up in June to the fastest pace since early 2023, adding to evidence of rising inflationary pressures that support the case for the Bank of Japan to keep raising interest rates.

item.title: OpenAI Executive Fidji Simo to Step Down Following Medical Leave
item.description: OpenAI executive Fidji Simo, the startup’s chief executive officer of AGI deployment, is stepping down from her full-time role following a three-month medical leave.

item.title: Gold Steadies as Traders Weigh Mideast Fighting, Rate Outlook
item.description: Gold steadied, as investors weighed renewed fighting in the Middle East and the prospects for interest-rate hikes to combat stubborn inflation.

item.title: Peru Leaves Key Rate Unchanged as Inflation Spike Seen Fading
item.description: Peru’s central bank held its key interest rate at 4.25% for a tenth straight month on Thursday, betting that an uptick in inflation will prove temporary.

item.title: JPMorgan Builds AI Agents That Beat 60/40 Portfolio in Backtests
item.description: As investors increasingly turn to artificial intelligence for help with everything from stock picking to risk management, JPMorgan Chase & Co. has been testing whether a model can do something more ambitious: allocate money itself.

item.title: A Tiny Island Near Singapore Has Become Asia’s Hub for Russian Oil
item.description: At least $1.6 billion worth of Moscow’s diesel, fuel oil and other products has been funneled from Indonesia’s tiny Karimun into major markets across the region.

item.title: Nexchip Set to Debut in Hong Kong After $890 Million Listing
item.description: Nexchip Semiconductor Corp. is set to begin trading in Hong Kong on Friday after raising $890 million in a share sale, testing investor appetite for Chinese chipmakers after a deluge of offerings in the artificial intelligence industry.

item.title: China Gets Chance at Fiscal Rethink After Debt Cleanup Milestone
item.description: Chinese provinces are nearing a milestone in Beijing’s plan to refinance their crushing debts, allowing local officials to refocus efforts on raising funds for infrastructure projects despite limited room to offer more support to the economy.

item.title: Crypto Criminal Accused of Crypto Crimes Again, While in Jail
item.description: A convicted crypto criminal is in trouble for crypto criming again. While in jail.

item.title: Trump's Latest Power Play Threatens US Housing Relief Bill
item.description: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act could come into force this weekend barring another round of disruption from the president.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Gain After US Chipmakers Rally: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks looked poised to gain on Friday after a resurgence in giant chipmakers drove a rebound on Wall Street. Oil opened lower in early Friday trading.

item.title: Oil Steady at End of Volatile Week as Iran Talks Said to Go On
item.description: Oil steadied at the end of a bumpy week as talks between the US and Iran were said to be continuing despite a flare-up in fighting that drove a drop in traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Gates Heir’s Shopping App Took Credit for Sales It Didn’t Drive
item.description: Phia, an advertising startup co-founded by Phoebe Gates, daughter of billionaire Microsoft Corp. co-founder Bill Gates, bills itself as a “personal shopping assistant” that helps users find the lowest prices on a broad range of clothes and fashion accessories.

item.title: Activist Donerail Urges Beazer Homes to Engage With Suitors
item.description: Activist investor Donerail Group is urging the board of Beazer Homes USA Inc. to engage with potential buyers after rival homebuilder Dream Finders Homes Inc. boosted its takeover offer this week.
